note: Hand mapping of the area-level assessments (SEC-03, 04, 08, 09, 11, 12, 15, 16, 17, 21) to individual controls. Conservative: a control is listed only where the assessment text supports it. IU = IMPLEMENTED_UNVERIFIED, P = PARTIAL_EVIDENCE, G = GAP_CONFIRMED.

rows.finding: Central policy.ts decisions, deny by default (733 of 782 mutating and 520 of 533 GET route pairs answer 401 unauthenticated) and server-side enforcement through route().

One request context carries one selected role (hasMembershipRole needs roles.length === 1; narrowToActiveRole selects none when several are held and none is chosen). No fallback to the highest-priority role.
A Super Admin acts as the platform admin only with no selected membership (isSuperAdmin requires membership === null); platform scope is a separate admin-scope cookie that now expires after 4 hours.

Step-up (15-minute fresh login) on role and permission changes; authorization re-read from the database on every request; persisted-actor re-check inside protected write transactions; a revoked selected role is refused (membership.role.manage).

33 named permissions for about 1,200 handlers (coarse; 118 handlers name one); role changes audited; role-by-route matrix baseline committed (fails when a role gains a route) but not every unauthorized role/action pair is tested.

Each role reaches a distinct role-shaped set of routes (matrix: learner 23, faculty 15, mentor 18, college admin 72, TPO 51 readable static GET routes on dev). Faculty and mentor scope to assigned sections and projects is enforced in services but not re-probed with seeded assignments.
Same-college horizontal probe: 144 requests by a learner for other learners' ids, 108 x 403, 28 x 400, 4 x 404, no foreign data.

Route inventory by the sweeps (533 GET and 782 mutating pairs), every route classified by route() auth mode, unauthenticated calls answer 401, role matrix finds function-level gaps, and the security:central ratchet fails a new route without classification.

Cross-college probe: 120 GET routes called with another college's ids returned no foreign data (59 x 404, 37 x 403); failure semantics are consistent (wrong role 403, foreign id 404, plain errors mapped centrally).
route() applies origin check, bounded body, rate limit and CSRF-equivalent same-origin enforcement before the handler.

Partial: about 1,086 service-enforced handlers check roles and ownership in services (43 easy to convert to named permissions); Zod strictObject bodies are the pattern but not measured; mutating methods not probed with foreign ids (database policies refuse cross-college writes).
One registry names every machine secret and key (21 entries) with kind, length and distinctness rules; CI workflows reject newly committed credentials and credential artifacts.

Secrets live in Kubernetes Secrets, never in git; startup and readiness logs name a secret without its value; production readiness fails closed on an invalid configuration; incident runbook exists. Not a managed secret store; history scan not done.

Open: the GCP key and production database password rotation is owner-only; no rotation runbook per secret, no rotation test, no key versioning (rotating DB10_OUTBOUND_ENCRYPTION_KEY_BASE64 needs re-encryption).
Response headers on every dev response: CSP with frame-ancestors none, X-Frame-Options DENY, Permissions-Policy denying camera, microphone, geolocation, payment and usb.

Nonce-based script CSP is built and switched on for dev (CSP_NONCE=on) with no violations on the pages checked; style-src still allows unsafe-inline; COOP same-origin-allow-popups and Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy same-origin on private API responses.

File access is decided from rows (owner, college, resource), signed GET URLs are short-lived (5-minute ceiling), content type is checked by magic bytes after upload (mismatch QUARANTINED), size ceilings per kind.

Signed URLs bind scope and object keys include the owner scope; malware scanning is designed fail-closed (upload stays VERIFYING until a scanner posts a CLEAN verdict) but no scanner is chosen or deployed.
The private bucket does not exist: the legacy R2 key is object-scoped and the legacy bucket is public, so private uploads answer STORAGE_NOT_CONFIGURED (owner: create lms-vnext-private).
Inbound machine endpoints verify an HMAC or shared secret over the raw body in constant time, refuse a browser Origin, bound the body, and use strict schemas.

Provider list known; separate credentials per provider on dev; signatures cover the body but not a timestamp (inbound mail is idempotent by providerMessageId; scan verdicts are bound to file, college and generation); calendar tokens are encrypted before storage.

Every internal route goes through internalRoute(): browser Origin refused, query string refused, one named secret per route compared with timingSafeEqual, a missing or short server secret denies every call.

Jobs run in a named system scope and take college_id from the rows they process (no caller-supplied tenant); dispatch uses delivery keys with a shared claim store; denials are audited as internal.denied without the credential. Machine calls have no timestamp or nonce.

Cloud SQL on private IP; NetworkPolicy lms-vnext-ingress-from-lb-only; vNext pod non-root (uid 1001), RuntimeDefault seccomp, no privilege escalation, read-only root filesystem, all capabilities dropped, CPU and memory limits, service-account token not mounted.
No egress NetworkPolicy exists: the pod can reach any address.

Google load balancer with pre-shared certificates and HSTS; deployment manifests are version controlled; /e2e/* now 404 on production builds while /api/internal/* stays reachable behind secrets (owner decision).
Cloud SQL forty-two-prod-1 has automatic daily backups, 7-day point-in-time recovery and deletion protection (recorded 2026-10-14); nothing proved by a restore.
No recovery point or recovery time targets are defined and no restore test has been done (owner decision on cost).

Incident response runbook (draft 2026-11-08): roles and the first 15 minutes, where evidence is, containment steps, credential compromise, cross-college exposure, recovery and notification. Written, not rehearsed; credential rotation has no per-secret tooling or key versioning.
No on-call rota or emergency contact roster beyond the owner, and no tabletop exercise or rehearsal has been run (runbook section 7).
data-inventory.md lists the 96 tables holding personal or sensitive columns by class; no written sensitivity level per class and processors are not yet recorded.
Open (owner and legal): lawful basis and purpose, retention by category, and a data-subject request flow for correction, deletion and export do not exist yet.

CI database job runs scripts/rls-tenant-acceptance.mjs as a non-superuser role in inert and enforce modes against a disposable PostgreSQL service; security workflows are path-triggered; adversarial fixtures use dedicated disposable databases.

Role-by-route matrix, cross-college probe (120 routes) and same-college probe (144 requests) exist as committed scripts with evidence, but run against dev by hand rather than in CI; catalog and runtime-principal probes cover privilege drift; webhook signatures are tested, replay is not; skipped database suites and missing branch protection mean a failing critical test does not yet block a release.

security_audit_events is append-only: a trigger refuses UPDATE, DELETE and TRUNCATE and the runtime role is refused them (verified on dev 2026-11-08). Not hash-chained, so tamper evidence stops at the database privileges.

Anomaly tripwire flags repeated denials, login probing, id enumeration and bulk export bursts and reports them to the structured log and the alert module; regression suites exist for earlier incidents (cross-college, role fixtures) but are not grouped as an incident suite.

Super Admin sign-in is two OTP codes (no hardware-backed or phishing-resistant factor), and there is no two-person or independent approval for Super Admin assignment or other high-impact platform operations (owner decision pending).

Anomaly tripwire (src/security/anomaly.ts) flags 20 denials per 5 minutes per user, 10 login probes per 5 minutes per client tag, 30 not-found answers per 5 minutes per user (object enumeration) and 10 exports per 10 minutes per user; findings go to the structured log, the alert module and security_audit_events. Fired as designed on dev.

Denied internal machine calls are written as internal.denied without the credential; log retention and minimisation for the audit table are not defined (audit rows carry no contacts or codes, only user ids and one-way IP tags).

A sign-in from a device name and agent not seen before records auth.new_device; per-IP and per-account limits exist for sign-in; login events are written to the append-only audit table. No risk score or step-up on a suspicious sign-in yet.
Bulk exports require step-up (15-minute fresh login), are audited as api.export events and feed the bulk-export tripwire.

Rich text goes through a strict rebuild (sanitizeCourseDisplayHtml in src/modules/courses/course-display-validation.ts): all text is escaped, only a short tag allowlist is reconstructed and every attribute is dropped. Only 8 files use dangerouslySetInnerHTML: 3 course components fed by that sanitizer and 5 static marketing/policy pages. Unit tests: course-display-content.test.ts and chat7-superadmin-course-authoring-break.test.ts.
No client code builds HTML from location, hash or query; the CSP (nonce scripts, connect-src 'self') blocks injected script, but no DOM-XSS scanner or Trusted Types is in place.
No Access-Control-Allow-* header is set anywhere in src, so browsers enforce same-origin; credentialed cross-origin access and wildcard CORS do not exist.
Search of src for secrets in query strings (token, otp, password, secret, code) finds none; share and invite tokens travel in the path and are stored hashed, sign-in codes only in POST bodies.

Browser storage holds interface preferences only (table columns and sort, recent searches, last selected college or membership key, a sign-out broadcast key); no token, code or personal data. Sign-out writes lms:signout so other tabs leave, the session cookie is HttpOnly and server-revoked.
No third-party script tags or analytics widgets in src; the only third-party content is the YouTube iframe API for lesson video. No subresource integrity or formal inventory of embeds.
Authorization is enforced in route() and the services; the role-by-route matrix and unauthenticated gate test the server regardless of what the UI hides.

Upload types are an allowlist (src/modules/storage/file-policy.ts: documents, three image types, zip for some flows; no HTML, SVG or executables). Signed links force attachment unless the type is a PDF or png/jpeg/gif/webp, filenames are ASCII-cleaned and percent-encoded in Content-Disposition, and responses carry private, no-store.

Zip is accepted for some flows but the server never extracts uploads, there are no conversion or preview workers, and object keys are opaque and scope-prefixed rather than user paths. Nothing is proved by a hostile-archive or traversal test.

File access is decided from database rows (owner, college, resource) at every signed-URL request, with a 5-minute ceiling, so ended memberships stop working on the next request; same-college learner probe found no foreign data.
Signed links are short-lived; the legacy bucket is public (see SEC-11-001). Bulk exports are audited as api.export events; individual file downloads are not yet audited.
No retention or deletion policy is defined for submitted documents (owner and legal decision; SEC-22).

scripts/rls-tenant-acceptance.mjs (34 checks, run in the CI database job as a non-superuser role) covers read, insert, update, delete, moving a row to another college, derived child rows with a foreign parent and the no-scope case in enforce mode (no rows visible); scripts/rls-isolation-sweep.mjs ran 619 checks on dev.

Runtime principal probe on dev: not superuser, no BYPASSRLS, no CREATEROLE or CREATEDB, no role memberships, owns 0 of 278 tables, cannot TRUNCATE or CREATE; 0 SECURITY DEFINER functions exist (asserted by the acceptance script), so there is no search_path hazard in privileged functions.

Migrations run as lms_vnext_migrator (secret vnext-db-migrator) and the web Deployment as lms_vnext_app; jobs run in named system scopes. Worker and migrator privileges are not tested separately by a dedicated test.
scripts/rls-perf-probe.mjs measured the policies on dev within the agreed budget before enforcement was switched on (docs/security/rls-rollout.md).

Row-level security narrows counts, filters and aggregates because it applies inside the database; foreign ids answer 404 and the per-user not-found tripwire flags id walks. Users holding several memberships work through one selected membership per request; no dedicated test for an admin in one college and a learner in another.
No external search index exists; search runs as SQL under row-level security.
Cross-college authority exists only as the Super Admin admin-scope, which is selected explicitly, expires after 4 hours and writes an audit event.

One policy interface (src/modules/permissions/policy.ts: can and requirePermission with college, organization and resource arguments) is used by route(); roles are the fixed MEMBERSHIP_ROLES constant, so there is no editable role catalogue to bypass.

Conditions and relationships (assignment, project membership, recruiter grants) are enforced in services; self-lockout and protected-admin targets are guarded and tested (assertMutableMembershipTarget); bulk role changes need step-up; src/security is code-owned but branch protection is off so review is not enforced.
No separation of duties or two-person approval for especially sensitive operations (owner decision).
Request bodies are strict Zod objects in most routes (unknown keys rejected); API-initiated background work runs in a named system scope and takes tenant ids from rows, not from the caller.
Sign-in proves control of the contact: a one-time code is sent to the phone or email and consumed once (identity_auth_attempts, used_at, HMAC digests) before a session exists.
Sign-in start answers differently for an unknown contact (404) than for a known one, which allows account enumeration; fixing it is a product decision (owner action list).

The only authenticator is a one-time code to a verified contact, so there is no enrolment, replacement or removal flow and no SSO linking to protect; recovery is the same code flow. This changes the moment passkeys or MFA are added.

Faculty grade and submission access re-checks the persisted teaching assignment inside the write transaction (assertPersistedFacultyTeachingMutation), learners reach only their own submissions (same-college probe: 144 requests, no foreign data), and published grades are immutable in the database fixtures.

Lesson access follows enrolment rows; grading actions write activity events inside the transaction (recordActivityEventInTransaction). No entitlement-bypass test per lesson type and no grade-override report.

Recruiter access to learner profiles runs through relationship-scoped grants that must be ACTIVE, VERIFIED and unexpired for an ACTIVE company-college relationship at sign-in and at use; the CI job 'DB017 relationship-scoped disclosure defaults' tests the negative and tenant cases.
vNext issues no learner certificates today (only staff identity documents), so there is nothing to forge; revisit if certificates are added.
data-inventory.md lists the 96 tables holding personal data; API responses are built per route and some return whole rows. Field-level response review is not done.

The secret registry records a purpose for every entry; the workflow 'Security - full-history secret scan' scans all history; cryptography is node:crypto (AES-256-GCM, HMAC-SHA256, randomBytes, timingSafeEqual), no home-made primitives.
Dev has its own generated secrets in vnext-keys; the production secrets were not touched or compared here. The R2 key is the legacy object-scoped key and provider keys are not scoped per environment.
The runtime uses static database and provider credentials in Kubernetes Secrets (no workload identity), and keys are not held in a managed KMS; provider-default encryption at rest only.

Providers and the data class sent to each are partly listed in data-inventory.md; outbound fetches go through guarded helpers (recruiter ZIP SSRF boundary has its own workflow) but cloud-metadata blocking is not tested; provider results never choose the actor; emergency disablement exists only as flags (MAINTENANCE_MODE, PRIVATE_STORAGE_SCANNER_READY, module access rules).

Scan verdicts must match file id, college id and generation; inbound mail is idempotent by providerMessageId and deliveries claim a key in the shared store (fails closed); structured logs name secrets and routes without values.
Internal routes accept only schema-bound, size-bounded bodies (or none) and refuse query strings.

Jobs run in named system scopes rather than a Super Admin identity and take college_id from the rows they process; per-job re-checks of revoked memberships and dead-letter handling were not reviewed for all eight services; denied calls are audited as internal.denied, there is no reprocessing tool to audit.
Workers and the web app share one runtime database role and pod identity; scheduler, mail, storage and analytics privileges are not separated.

The vNext pod runs non-root with a read-only root filesystem, dropped capabilities and RuntimeDefault seccomp; the same-origin check uses the actual Host header, never X-Forwarded-Host, and forwarded client addresses are hardened for rate limits.

Database roles are split (runtime and migrator); images are not scanned or pinned by digest in the manifest; dev and production use separate namespaces and secrets; the schema-drift CI job and Dependabot exist but there is no cluster drift detection or image scan.
No workload identity for cloud access and no compromised-workload isolation test.
/ready reports database and configuration health and error-level logs reach the Telegram alert module; rate limiting degrades to per-process memory when the shared store is down.
A failed dependency never opens an authorization fallback: database errors deny, the shared store claim fails closed, and only rate limiting degrades (availability, not access).
No restore test, backup integrity check, corruption or ransomware scenario, restoration runbook or outage test exists (restore test is an owner cost decision).

Thousands of unit tests plus integration suites in CI cover sign-in, role selection (narrowToActiveRole, identity-system-roles), account disable and membership revocation (db01-session-atomic-authorization, workflow 'session idle and atomic role-change revocation'), same-origin checks on route() and concurrency races (revoke-versus-write serialization tests in the database job).

Cross-organization and forbidden-field cases exist route by route; the course sanitizer and the sql-raw-dynamic ratchet cover injection; a one-time code is consumed once (db01-login-consume tests) but a dedicated OTP replay suite, cache and job isolation tests and provider-failure tests are not written.
No independent testing has been commissioned and no coordinated-disclosure contact (security.txt) is published; both need the owner (timing, budget and a monitored security address).

Security findings are tracked in docs/tracker.json: a control only moves with exact commit and passing-run evidence, VERIFIED needs an independent reviewer, and negative invariant tests enforce this in CI.

Partial governance artefacts exist: accepted-risks.md and OWNER-ACTIONS.md act as the risk register, central-security-architecture.md and the ratchet guards act as the coding standard, CODEOWNERS and CI gate changes (branch protection is off), UX guard waivers carry expiry dates, and docs/security/evidence plus the tracker are the audit evidence trail.

Organisational controls not established: security ownership beyond the owner, access reviews, separation of production and development access, MFA enforcement on source control and cloud, vendor reviews, policy review cadence and training (owner decisions).

Not built or not done: just-in-time privileged access, a reviewed emergency-access procedure, contextual risk scoring, red-team exercises, continuous attack-surface monitoring, security chaos tests and independent verification of the critical controls.

Issued credentials are HMAC-signed (sessions, share proofs, reply tokens) with keys from the registry; the share-proof key is now separable from AUTH_SECRET. No asymmetric signing or key rotation scheme.

The incident runbook has no severity levels, no playbooks for unauthorized database access, compromised storage objects or malicious integrations, no legal notification analysis, no root-cause review process and no detection/containment/recovery timing (runbook section 7).

Emergency disabling exists as flags (MAINTENANCE_MODE, PRIVATE_STORAGE_SCANNER_READY, module access rules, user disable); the runbook lists where evidence lives and says not to delete anything, without a forensic procedure.

Candidate discovery by recruiters depends on explicit relationship grants (ACTIVE, VERIFIED, unexpired, capability-scoped) and share defaults tested in the CI job 'DB017 relationship-scoped disclosure defaults'.

Sharing between colleges and recruiters is recorded in grant and relationship tables; vendor data classes are only partly listed; whether the NSRIT data on dev is real students is unanswered (owner action 16); Cloud SQL runs in asia-south1 (India) but residency is not documented.
Minors' data handling, secure disposal, counsel review of Indian and international obligations and customer-specific obligations are not done (owner and legal).
vNext has no billing or payment workflow today, so there is nothing to validate; revisit if one is added.

The only cross-request, process-level cache in src is the skill catalog search cache (src/modules/skills/catalog-service.ts: 256 entries, 20 second TTL, keyed by query mode, text, category and limit); the skill catalog is platform-wide reference data and authorization happens in the route before it is read. All other Maps are per-request locals and no Next data cache (unstable_cache, force-cache, revalidate) is used.

383 unique indexes exist; many are scoped by department or college (for example courses_active_department_name_trim_uq), but some are global (courses_slug_uq), so uniqueness is not consistently tenant-scoped.

Faculty attendance and schedule writes re-check the persisted teaching assignment inside the transaction and are bounded to the active delivery (COURSES-BREAK-FACULTY-14 and the attendance integration suites); no fraud-pattern detection beyond that.
